name: Moong Dal Khichdi
cuisine: Gujarati / pan-Indian home food (the plain yellow-dal khichdi of Gujarati and Marwari homes in Mumbai, eaten with kadhi and papad)

ingredients.name: Split yellow moong dal (dhuli moong dal)
Raw rice (sona masoori or any short/medium grain)
Ghee
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 tsp for tempering + 1 tsp to drizzle)

equipment: Bowl and strainer for washing and soaking the rice and dal
Ladle (a potato masher or the back of a steel tumbler also works for mashing)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teacup and teaspoons are fine stand-ins)
Small spoon for the ghee drizzle

steps.title: Measure the dal
steps.text: Put 40 g (about 3 tbsp) split yellow moong dal in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of pale-yellow split lentils.
steps.cameraCheck: The moong dal in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Yellow dal pouring from a spoon into a steel bowl.

steps.title: Add the rice
steps.text: Add 40 g (about 3 tbsp) raw rice to the same bowl.
steps.visualCue: Roughly equal amounts of white rice and yellow dal.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice and dal in the bowl

steps.title: Wash
steps.text: Cover with water, rub gently with your fingers and drain. Repeat 2 more times.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is only slightly cloudy and no froth floats on top.
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl with the last rinse water
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling rice and dal in cloudy water.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover with fresh water and leave for 15 min, then drain fully.
steps.tip: Soaking gives a creamier khichdi and fewer whistles. Short of time? Skip it and give 1 extra whistle in step 11.
steps.visualCue: The grains look plumper and paler.
steps.cameraCheck: The drained rice and dal in the strainer

steps.title: Heat the ghee
steps.text: Put the open cooker on low heat and add 1 tsp (5 g) ghee.
steps.cameraCheck: The melted ghee in the cooker
steps.videoShot: A spoon of ghee melting in the cooker base.

steps.title: Add cumin and pepper
steps.text: Add ½ tsp cumin seeds and 4–5 peppercorns.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black, it has burnt; wipe out and start again, or it will taste bitter.
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles and darkens one shade and smells toasty.

steps.title: Add hing
steps.text: Add a small pinch of hing and stir once.
steps.videoShot: A pinch of hing dropping into the ghee.

steps.title: Add rice and dal
steps.text: Add the drained rice and dal and stir gently on low heat.
steps.visualCue: The grains are coated in ghee and the wet look has gone.
steps.videoShot: A ladle turning the grains in the ghee.

steps.title: Add turmeric and salt
steps.text: Sprinkle in ¼ tsp turmeric powder and 1.8 g (a scant ⅓ tsp) salt. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn evenly pale yellow.
steps.cameraCheck: The yellow grains in the cooker

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in 320 ml (about 1⅓ cups) water. Stir and scrape the bottom so nothing sticks.
steps.tip: 4 parts water gives a soft, spoonable khichdi; use 3 parts (240 ml) for a firmer, mushy-rice style.
steps.visualCue: The water stands about 3 cm above the grains; the bottom is clean.
steps.cameraCheck: The open cooker with water and grains
steps.videoShot: Water pouring in and a ladle scraping the base.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Close the lid and cook on medium heat for 4 whistles (5 if you skipped the soak), then switch off.
steps.tip: The ghee tempering helps stop moong dal frothing into the whistle. Keep the heat at medium, not high.
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the stove
steps.videoShot: Steam puffing out with a whistle.

steps.title: Let the pressure drop
steps.text: Leave the cooker closed until the pressure falls on its own.
steps.visualCue: The weight lifts easily with no hiss.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooker with the lid off
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off to show steaming yellow khichdi.

steps.title: Mash and loosen
steps.text: Mash lightly with the ladle, add 50 ml hot water, stir and simmer on low for 1 min. Add up to 30 ml more if it looks thick.
steps.tip: Khichdi thickens a lot as it stands; leave it a little looser than you want to eat it.
steps.visualCue: Soft and creamy; it slowly drops off the ladle, with grains still visible.
steps.cameraCheck: A ladle of khichdi lifted from the cooker
steps.videoShot: The ladle pressing and stirring the khichdi.

steps.title: Taste
steps.text: Taste and add a pinch of salt only if needed.
steps.videoShot: A spoon tasting from the pot.

steps.title: Serve with ghee
steps.text: Spoon into a bowl and drizzle the remaining 1 tsp (5 g) ghee on top.
steps.visualCue: A yellow, glossy bowl with a pool of melting ghee.
steps.cameraCheck: The served bowl with ghee on top
steps.videoShot: Ghee drizzled onto a hot bowl of khichdi, with kadhi and papad beside it.

reasons: boiled, one-pot, no onion, garlic, added sugar or deep frying; the 1:1 rice-to-moong ratio gives about 13 g protein and 5 g fibre for about 365 kcal, and moong dal is easy to digest, which is why khichdi is the classic recovery meal. Against it: it is still mostly white-rice starch with a high glycaemic response, low in vegetables and vitamin C, and the ghee brings about 29% of the day's saturated fat. Restaurant versions often use a butter or ghee-heavy tadka, more salt, and come with kadhi and a fried papad, which add fat and a lot of sodium.

researchRating.basis: a near-universal Indian comfort food, especially in Gujarati, Rajasthani and North Indian homes, with very well-reviewed recipes (Swasthi's / Indian Healthy Recipes khichdi 4.99/5 from 457 votes; Hebbar's Kitchen 4.97 from about 247 ratings) and enough demand to support khichdi-only delivery brands in Mumbai (One Dollar Khichdi, Khichdi By Protein Chef, Great Indian Khichdi, Khichdi Dreamz). Deduction because many people see plain khichdi as bland "sick-day food" and prefer masala khichdi or pongal when eating out.

storage: Best fresh; it sets firm as it cools. Fridge: up to 2 days in an airtight box, within 2 hours of cooking. Freezer: up to 1 month, though the texture turns slightly grainy. To reheat, add 2–3 tbsp hot water, cover and microwave for 1–2 min, stirring halfway, or warm in a covered pan on low heat for 3–4 min, stirring.
leftoverRemix: Khichdi parathas. Knead 1 cup cold leftover khichdi with about ½ cup whole-wheat flour (atta), ¼ tsp ajwain, a pinch of chilli powder and 1 tbsp chopped coriander into a soft dough (no water needed), roll into 3 parathas and cook on a hot tawa with ½ tsp ghee or oil per side until golden spots appear. Serve with curd and pickle: soft porridge turned into a chewy, spiced flatbread. (Adds gluten; not for the gluten-free variant.)
burnOff: about 5.2 km of running (365 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 7.3 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 28 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With kadhi and a roasted papad (about +135–170 kcal), add about 2–2.5 km of running.

navratri.reason: rice and moong dal (a grain and a pulse) are avoided on the common North and West Indian Navratri vrat rule set; samak-rice or sabudana khichdi is the usual vrat swap, but that is a different dish

ekadashi.reason: rice and all dals, including moong, are the main foods given up on Ekadashi

jain.reason: no onion, garlic, potato or other roots; rice, moong dal, ghee, cumin, hing and dried turmeric fit common Jain practice (Jain dal khichdi is a standard menu item, e.g. K Bhagat Tarachand, Borivali)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal concern; soft, mild and filling with moong dal protein and slow-release starch, which suits sehri; salt is moderate, about 1.8 g in the bowl

jain.reason: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other fresh root; uses dried turmeric powder and hing, both widely used in Jain kitchens (some families also avoid turmeric powder; views vary)

vegan.reason: use 2 tsp groundnut oil or coconut oil instead of ghee

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: no onion or garlic; the flavour comes from ghee, cumin, hing and turmeric

glutenFree.reason: rice and moong dal are gluten-free, but most hing (asafoetida) sold in India is compounded with wheat flour; use a hing labelled gluten-free or leave it out

dairyFree.reason: ghee is the only dairy; replace it with groundnut or coconut oil

description: A vegetarian, Jain and sattvik (no onion, no garlic) one-pot rice and yellow moong dal khichdi with ghee; vegan, gluten-free and dairy-free versions below.

variants.reason: . Main recipe already Jain (no onion, garlic, ginger or potato). Jain dal khichdi is also an established menu item (K Bhagat Tarachand, Borivali, Swiggy, ₹330). Families that avoid turmeric powder can leave it out; the khichdi is then pale, like pongal.
